_comment: Drafts of 2026-10-15 for the owner's and his priest's read: who wrote each book as the Church holds it, when, and what it is about. Nothing here is final until they approve it.

genesis.by: Moses, as the Church receives it
genesis.about: God creates the world and humanity, and after the fall calls Abraham and his family.

exodus.by: Moses, as the Church receives it
exodus.about: God frees Israel from Egypt through Moses and gives the Law at Sinai.

leviticus.by: Moses, as the Church receives it
leviticus.about: Israel receives the laws of sacrifice, priesthood, purity and the great Day of Atonement.

numbers.by: Moses, as the Church receives it
numbers.about: Israel wanders forty years in the wilderness between Sinai and the promised land.

deuteronomy.by: Moses, as the Church receives it
deuteronomy.about: Moses renews the covenant with Israel on the plains of Moab before his death.

joshua.when: Tradition: after the conquest of Canaan
joshua.about: Joshua leads Israel across the Jordan into the promised land and divides it among the tribes.

judges.about: Israel falls away again and again, and God raises up judges to deliver it.

ruth.about: A Moabite widow's faithfulness brings her into Israel and into the line of David.

1-samuel.by: Tradition: Samuel, then Nathan and Gad
1-samuel.about: Samuel anoints Saul as Israel's first king, then David, the shepherd who defeats Goliath.

2-samuel.by: Tradition: the prophets Nathan and Gad
2-samuel.about: David reigns over Israel, receives God's promise of an everlasting throne, sins, and repents.

1-kings.when: Completed in the Exile, 6th century BC
1-kings.about: Solomon builds the Temple, the kingdom divides, and Elijah stands against Ahab and Jezebel.

2-kings.when: Completed in the Exile, after 561 BC
2-kings.about: Elisha succeeds Elijah, and both kingdoms fall, Israel to Assyria and Judah to Babylon.

1-chronicles.about: Genealogies from Adam lead to David, whose reign is retold with care for worship.

2-chronicles.about: The kings of Judah are traced from Solomon's Temple to the exile and Cyrus's decree.

1-esdras.about: It retells the return from exile and adds the contest of three guardsmen of Darius.

ezra.by: Ezra the priest and scribe, as tradition holds
ezra.about: The exiles return from Babylon, rebuild the Temple, and are taught the law by Ezra.

nehemiah.by: Nehemiah, largely in his own words
nehemiah.about: Nehemiah rebuilds the walls of Jerusalem, and the people hear the law and renew the covenant.

tobit.by: Unknown; partly in Tobit's own voice
tobit.about: The archangel Raphael guides young Tobias, frees Sara from a demon, and heals Tobit.

judith.about: A devout widow saves her besieged town by slaying the enemy general Holofernes.

esther.about: Queen Esther risks her life to save her people from Haman's plot to destroy them.

1-maccabees.about: Mattathias and his sons lead the revolt against Antiochus and rededicate the Temple.

2-maccabees.about: It retells the revolt and honors the martyrs who died rather than break God's law.

3-maccabees.about: God rescues the Jews of Egypt from King Ptolemy's persecution through prayer and angels.

job.when: Uncertain; set in the age of the patriarchs
job.about: A righteous man loses everything, wrestles with God's justice, and is answered and restored.

psalms.by: King David and other inspired psalmists
psalms.when: 10th century BC to after the Exile
psalms.about: The Church's prayer book gathers psalms of praise, lament, repentance and prophecy of Christ.

proverbs.when: From Solomon, 10th century BC, gathered later
proverbs.about: Short sayings teach wisdom for daily life, beginning with the fear of the Lord.

ecclesiastes.about: The Preacher finds everything under the sun fleeting and calls the reader to fear God.

song-of-solomon.about: A bride and bridegroom sing of their love, which the Church reads as God's love.

wisdom.about: In Solomon's voice, the book praises divine Wisdom and the hope of the righteous.

sirach.by: Jesus son of Sirach; Greek by his grandson
sirach.about: A Jerusalem sage gathers wisdom for the whole of life and praises the famous fathers.

hosea.about: Hosea's marriage to an unfaithful wife mirrors God's faithful love for unfaithful Israel.

amos.by: The prophet Amos, a herdsman of Tekoa
amos.about: A herdsman from Judah denounces Israel's injustice and false worship, and foretells David's restored house.

micah.about: Micah condemns Judah's corrupt leaders and foretells the ruler to be born in Bethlehem.

joel.by: The prophet Joel, son of Bethuel
joel.about: A locust plague calls Judah to fasting, and God promises to pour out His Spirit.

obadiah.when: Tradition: Ahab's time; many say after 586 BC
obadiah.about: In one chapter, Obadiah condemns Edom for gloating over the fall of Jerusalem.

jonah.by: The prophet Jonah, as tradition holds
jonah.about: Jonah flees God's call, is swallowed by a great fish, and Nineveh repents.

nahum.about: Nahum foretells the fall of Nineveh, the cruel capital of Assyria.

habakkuk.about: Habakkuk questions God about evil and learns that the just will live by faith.

zephaniah.about: Zephaniah warns of the day of the Lord and promises joy to a humble remnant.

haggai.about: Haggai stirs the returned exiles to finish rebuilding the Temple.

zechariah.about: Visions encourage the rebuilding of the Temple and foretell the lowly King coming to Zion.

malachi.about: Malachi rebukes careless worship and promises a messenger before the great day of the Lord.

isaiah.about: Isaiah calls Judah to repentance and foretells the Virgin's Son and the Suffering Servant.

jeremiah.by: The prophet Jeremiah, with his scribe Baruch
jeremiah.about: Jeremiah warns Jerusalem of its fall, suffers for it, and foretells a new covenant.

baruch.by: Baruch, Jeremiah's scribe, as tradition holds
baruch.about: Exiles in Babylon confess their sins, praise God's Wisdom, and hope for return.

lamentations.by: The prophet Jeremiah, as tradition holds
lamentations.when: Soon after Jerusalem fell in 586 BC
lamentations.about: Five poems mourn the destruction of Jerusalem by Babylon in 586 BC.

epistle-of-jeremiah.when: Tradition: eve of the Exile; perhaps later
epistle-of-jeremiah.about: A letter warns the exiles that the idols of Babylon are no gods.

ezekiel.by: The prophet Ezekiel, a priest in exile
ezekiel.about: A priest in exile sees God's glory, foretells Jerusalem's fall, and promises new life.

daniel.by: The prophet Daniel, as the Church receives it
daniel.when: Tradition: 6th century BC; some say later
daniel.about: Daniel stays faithful in Babylon and sees visions of God's kingdom and the Son of Man.

prayer-of-manasseh.by: Ascribed to King Manasseh of Judah
prayer-of-manasseh.about: The penitent king of Judah confesses his sins and begs God's mercy.

2-esdras.when: About AD 100; Christian chapters added later
2-esdras.about: Ezra questions God about the fall of Jerusalem and is shown visions of the end.

matthew.when: Tradition: the first Gospel, before AD 70
matthew.about: Matthew presents Jesus as the promised Messiah, Son of David, who fulfills the Law.

mark.by: St Mark, from St Peter's preaching
mark.about: The shortest Gospel tells swiftly of Christ, the Son of God, and His Passion.

luke.by: St Luke, companion of St Paul
luke.about: Luke tells of Christ, the Savior of all, with special care for the poor and outcast.

john.about: John reveals Christ as the eternal Word made flesh, through His signs and discourses.

acts.about: The Holy Spirit descends at Pentecost and the apostles carry the Gospel from Jerusalem to Rome.

romans.about: Paul sets out the gospel of salvation by grace through faith for Jew and Gentile.

1-corinthians.about: Paul answers a divided church on unity, holiness, the Eucharist, love and the resurrection.

2-corinthians.about: Paul defends his apostolic ministry and boasts only in his weakness and in Christ.

galatians.when: Around AD 49, though some date it later
galatians.about: Paul defends the gospel of grace and Christian freedom against those requiring circumcision.

ephesians.about: Paul unfolds God's plan to unite all things in Christ and the Church as His body.

philippians.about: From prison Paul writes of joy and of Christ who humbled Himself to the Cross.

colossians.about: Paul proclaims Christ as the image of God and head of the Church, above all powers.

1-thessalonians.by: St Paul, with Silvanus and Timothy
1-thessalonians.about: Paul encourages a young church under persecution and comforts them about the departed.

2-thessalonians.by: St Paul, with Silvanus and Timothy
2-thessalonians.when: About AD 51, soon after the first
2-thessalonians.about: Paul corrects confusion about the Lord's coming and urges the faithful to keep working.

1-timothy.when: About AD 63, after his first imprisonment
1-timothy.about: Paul instructs Timothy on prayer, church order, sound teaching and the danger of riches.

2-timothy.by: St Paul, shortly before his martyrdom
2-timothy.when: About AD 67, from prison in Rome
2-timothy.about: Paul's last letter charges Timothy to guard the faith and endure, as his own end nears.

titus.about: Paul instructs Titus on appointing elders in Crete and on the grace that saves.

philemon.about: Paul asks Philemon to welcome back his runaway slave Onesimus as a brother in Christ.

hebrews.by: St Paul, as the Church receives it
hebrews.about: Christ, the eternal High Priest, fulfills and surpasses the worship of the Old Covenant.

james.by: St James, brother of the Lord
james.about: James teaches that living faith shows itself in works, mercy and the control of the tongue.

1-peter.about: Peter encourages suffering Christians with the living hope of the resurrection.

2-peter.by: St Peter, as the Church receives it
2-peter.when: Shortly before his martyrdom, about AD 67
2-peter.about: Peter's farewell calls the faithful to grow in virtue and to await the Lord's coming.

1-john.about: John calls believers to walk in the light and to love one another, as God loves.

2-john.by: St John, who calls himself the elder
2-john.about: The elder urges a church to walk in love and to reject deceivers.

3-john.by: St John, who calls himself the elder
3-john.about: The elder praises Gaius for his hospitality and rebukes the proud Diotrephes.

jude.by: St Jude, brother of the Lord
jude.about: Jude urges the faithful to defend the apostolic faith against ungodly intruders.

revelation.by: St John the Theologian, on Patmos
revelation.about: John's visions on Patmos unveil the Lamb's victory and the coming of the new Jerusalem.
